pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these gives the young plant its first food before its leaves open? (1 mark)
   A. The seed
   B. The wind
   C. The bark
   D. The flower

2. How do most flowering plants make new plants? (1 mark)
   A. By giving birth
   B. By seeds
   C. By laying eggs
   D. By walking away

3. What does the stem do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes food using sunlight
   B. Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   C. Only takes in water
   D. Makes seeds

4. Which part of the plant takes in water from the soil? (1 mark)
   A. Stem
   B. Flower
   C. Roots
   D. Seed coat

5. Why is a spider NOT an insect? (1 mark)
   A. It has a backbone
   B. It lives in water
   C. It has feathers
   D. It has eight legs, not six

6. Why is it important to protect wild animals and their homes? (1 mark)
   A. They do not need food
   B. They are dangerous to all people
   C. They can be sold cheaply
   D. They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya

7. Which of these is a sign of life in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Being painted
   B. Feeding
   C. Being made of metal
   D. Staying in one place forever

8. Which of these is a mammal that lives in water? (1 mark)
   A. Crocodile
   B. Tilapia
   C. Whale
   D. Frog

9. What is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal with hair
   B. An animal without a backbone
   C. An animal that flies
   D. An animal with a backbone

10. Which group of vertebrates feeds its young on milk? (1 mark)
   A. Mammals
   B. Birds
   C. Fish
   D. Reptiles

11. Where does digestion finish and digested food pass into the blood? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Small intestine
   C. Stomach
   D. Rectum

12. Which of these is a symptom of an unhealthy digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach ache
   B. Sneezing
   C. Sunburn
   D. A headache only

13. What is the correct order of parts food passes through? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach, mouth, gullet, small intestine
   B. Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine
   C. Mouth, stomach, gullet, anus
   D. Gullet, mouth, small intestine, stomach

14. Which of these solids can be poured? (1 mark)
   A. Stone
   B. Flour
   C. Ruler
   D. Brick

15. Why are solids like bricks and stones used to build houses? (1 mark)
   A. They are invisible
   B. They keep their shape and can support weight
   C. They spread out
   D. They flow easily

16. Which of these is true of a gas? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps its own shape
   B. It cannot spread out
   C. It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   D. It is always visible

17. Which of these can be a solid, liquid or gas depending on conditions? (1 mark)
   A. Wooden chair
   B. Water
   C. Book
   D. Stone

18. Which of these is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Steam
   B. Dirty bath water
   C. Smoke
   D. A banana peel

19. Which is the best order of managing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Burn, bury, throw
   B. Throw, burn, bury
   C. Recycle, reuse, reduce
   D. Reduce, reuse, recycle

20. What is the best way to deal with metal scrap in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it in a river
   B. Bury it in the school garden
   C. Burn it
   D. Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it

21. Why is it good to separate waste into different bins? (1 mark)
   A. It makes waste smell
   B. It makes waste burn
   C. It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   D. It makes waste heavier

22. What are the three Rs? (1 mark)
   A. Read, write and run
   B. Recycle, repair and rest
   C. Reduce, remove and rest
   D. Reduce, reuse and recycle

23. Which of these is non-decomposable? (1 mark)
   A. Fruit peel
   B. Plastic bottle
   C. Dung
   D. Dry leaves

24. A tap leaks 2 litres every hour. How much is wasted in 5 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 2 litres
   B. 7 litres
   C. 25 litres
   D. 10 litres

25. Which of these is a way of protecting water sources? (1 mark)
   A. Letting animals dirty the spring
   B. Planting trees near rivers
   C. Throwing waste in the river
   D. Washing clothes in the river

26. Who should monitor taps in a school? (1 mark)
   A. Water monitors
   B. Only cooks
   C. Nobody
   D. Only visitors

27. Why do we wash vegetables in a basin? (1 mark)
   A. It makes them heavier
   B. It makes them cold
   C. It wastes water
   D. It uses less water and the water can be reused

28. Which of these is true of water? (1 mark)
   A. Animals do not need water
   B. Only humans need water
   C. Plants do not need water
   D. Water is needed by all living things

29. A leaking pipe wastes 5 litres each day. How much is wasted in 7 days? (1 mark)
   A. 35 litres
   B. 57 litres
   C. 70 litres
   D. 12 litres

30. Why do matches light when rubbed on the box? (1 mark)
   A. Friction makes heat
   B. Gravity makes light
   C. Friction makes cold
   D. Wind makes fire

31. Which force pulls objects down towards the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. Wind
   B. Sound
   C. Gravity
   D. Friction

32. Why are tyres made with rough patterns? (1 mark)
   A. To make them lighter
   B. To grip the road
   C. To make them shiny
   D. To reduce friction

33. Why do houses have windows? (1 mark)
   A. To let in daylight
   B. To make noise
   C. To let in only rain
   D. To keep out light

34. What is a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. Something that reflects light
   B. Something that gives out its own light
   C. Something that blocks light
   D. Something that is dark

35. What does light help us to do? (1 mark)
   A. Hear
   B. Taste
   C. Smell
   D. See

36. If you smell gas from a cooker, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Turn on an electric switch
   B. Tell an adult and keep flames away
   C. Ignore it
   D. Light a match

37. Which of these uses electricity to make heat? (1 mark)
   A. Electric kettle
   B. Book
   C. Bicycle
   D. Wooden chair

38. Why does an ice cube melt in your hand? (1 mark)
   A. Cold goes into your hand
   B. The hand makes water
   C. Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   D. The ice makes heat

39. Why are cooking pots made of metal? (1 mark)
   A. Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   B. Metal does not get hot
   C. Metal is soft
   D. Metal is light

40. Which of these helps to prevent burns? (1 mark)
   A. Using gloves
   B. Playing near fire
   C. Touching hot pots
   D. Holding hot handles

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain what would happen to a young bean plant if all its leaves were removed and why. (4 marks)

42. Why is it wrong to say that a tree is not alive because it cannot walk? (3 marks)

43. Explain how light helps in security and safety. Give three examples. (3 marks)

44. Explain why friction can be both useful and a problem. Give two examples of each. (4 marks)

45. Explain why sand is not a liquid although it can be poured. (3 marks)

46. Explain why we should reduce friction in machines and how it can be done. (5 marks)

47. Name the three Rs of waste management. (2 marks)

48. Explain how a pupil can show that plants respond to light. (4 marks)

49. Describe the characteristics that show that animals are living things. Use examples. (5 marks)

50. Explain why deworming is important and state two other ways of preventing worms. (4 marks)

51. Describe how you would do an activity to show gravity. (4 marks)

52. Explain why a rainwater tank should have a lid. (3 marks)

53. Convert 3 litres into millilitres. (2 marks)

54. Describe what happens to food in the stomach. (3 marks)

55. Write two uses of each of these: solids, liquids and gases. (Choose any four uses in all.) (4 marks)

56. Describe how you would make a dustbin from locally available materials. (4 marks)

57. Explain how fibre helps the digestive system. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — The seed
   The seed contains stored food that feeds the young plant at first.

2. B — By seeds
   Most flowering plants reproduce by making seeds inside fruits.

3. B — Holds up the plant and carries water and food
   The stem supports the plant and carries water and food.

4. C — Roots
   Roots take in water and mineral salts.

5. D — It has eight legs, not six
   Insects have six legs and spiders have eight.

6. D — They are part of nature and bring visitors to Kenya
   Wild animals are part of our environment and bring income through tourism.

7. B — Feeding
   Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die.

8. C — Whale
   A whale breathes air and feeds milk to its calf, so it is a mammal even though it lives in water.

9. B — An animal without a backbone
   Invertebrates have no backbone.

10. A — Mammals
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

11. B — Small intestine
   The small intestine completes digestion and absorbs food into the blood.

12. A — Stomach ache
   Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation are digestive symptoms.

13. B — Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine
   Food goes from the mouth down the gullet to the stomach and then the small intestine.

14. B — Flour
   Flour is made of tiny solid grains that can pour.

15. B — They keep their shape and can support weight
   Solids keep their shape.

16. C — It has no fixed shape and no fixed volume
   A gas spreads to fill the space.

17. B — Water
   Water can be ice, liquid water or steam.

18. D — A banana peel
   A banana peel is a solid thrown away.

19. D — Reduce, reuse, recycle
   First make less waste, then reuse, then recycle.

20. D — Sell it to a scrap dealer or reuse it
   Metal can be recycled.

21. C — It makes reusing, recycling and composting easier
   Sorting helps each type be managed properly.

22. D — Reduce, reuse and recycle
   Reduce, reuse and recycle are ways of managing waste.

23. B — Plastic bottle
   Plastic does not rot easily.

24. D — 10 litres
   2 x 5 = 10 litres.

25. B — Planting trees near rivers
   Tree roots hold the soil and protect water.

26. A — Water monitors
   Monitors help make sure taps are closed.

27. D — It uses less water and the water can be reused
   A basin limits water use and allows reuse.

28. D — Water is needed by all living things
   All living things need water.

29. A — 35 litres
   5 x 7 = 35 litres.

30. A — Friction makes heat
   Rubbing produces heat.

31. C — Gravity
   Gravity pulls things towards the centre of the Earth.

32. B — To grip the road
   Grip needs friction.

33. A — To let in daylight
   Windows allow sunlight to enter the room.

34. B — Something that gives out its own light
   A source of light makes its own light.

35. D — See
   Light lets us see objects.

36. B — Tell an adult and keep flames away
   Gas can catch fire, so avoid flames.

37. A — Electric kettle
   A kettle is heated by electricity.

38. C — Heat goes from your hand into the ice
   Heat moves from the warm hand to the ice.

39. A — Metal passes heat quickly to the food
   Metal passes heat from the fire to the food.

40. A — Using gloves
   Gloves give protection.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant would become weak and stop growing. Leaves make food for the plant. Roots can take in water but without leaves the plant cannot make enough food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for weak or stops growing, 1 mark for leaves make food, 1 mark for no food made, 1 mark for roots alone are not enough.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plants show life in other ways. They grow, reproduce, respond, remove waste and die. Only some animals walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for stating plants show signs of life, 1 mark for naming signs, 1 mark for saying walking is not a sign needed for all living things.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Street lights help people see, security lights keep thieves away, traffic lights direct drivers, torches show dangers, reflectors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each example.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Useful: brakes stop bicycles and shoes grip the ground. A problem: it wears out tyres and makes machines hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it helps in some cases and harms in others, and 1 mark for each correct example up to 3.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each grain of sand is a small solid with its own shape. The grains are piled together and pour as a pile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for grains being solids, 1 mark for grains having shape, 1 mark for conclusion.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Friction wears out parts, wastes energy and makes machines hot. It is reduced by oiling, smoothing, using rollers or ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for methods.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put a plant in a box with a hole on one side. After some days the plant bends towards the hole showing it responds to light.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the set up, 1 mark for the hole giving light from one side, 1 mark for the plant bending, 1 mark for conclusion.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals feed, grow, breathe, reproduce, remove waste, move, respond and die. Give examples such as a goat eating grass and a hen laying eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign to a maximum of 5.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Worms live in the intestines and take food and make us weak. Deworming kills them. Wear shoes, wash hands, keep nails short.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 1 mark each for other ways.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drop a stone and a ball from the same height. Observe that they fall down to the ground. Gravity pulls them down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for items, 1 mark for dropping, 1 mark for observing downward fall, 1 mark for conclusion.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps out dirt and leaves and stops mosquitoes from breeding in it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirt, 1 mark for mosquitoes, 1 mark for making water safer.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3000 ml.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 3 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: The stomach churns the food and mixes it with strong juices. The juices kill many germs and break down the food into a thick soup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for churns, 1 mark for juices and 1 mark for germs or thick soup.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Solids: building, tools, clothes. Liquids: drinking, washing, cooking, fuel. Gases: breathing, cooking gas, inflating tyres.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct use up to 4.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a strong bucket, box or container. Cut and smooth the top and cover any sharp edge. Make a lid if possible. Paint a label saying waste only and put it in a suitable place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fibre in fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps food and waste move through the intestines and helps prevent constipation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming fibre foods, 1 mark for movement, 1 mark for constipation.
